name: Dennis Koshta
shortBio: I build AI systems, research model behavior, and make the evidence behind a result easier to inspect.
aboutParagraphs: I'm a software engineer based in San Francisco. My work spans language-model experiments, formal proofs, developer tools, and interactive software. The thread connecting them is a practical question: what would convince us that this actually works?

I like projects where an idea has to meet a concrete test: a proof checker, a held-out task, a preserved document, a reconciled order, or a user trying to make something. I also study the limits of those tests—what they measure, what they miss, and how model behavior changes around them.

I'm a Founding Software Engineer at Bronco AI. My public description of that work centers on evaluation: making agent performance measurable. This portfolio focuses on independent and open work, alongside earlier team research and systems projects.

I studied at the University of California, Santa Cruz, where my activities included NeuroTechSC and the Artificial Intelligence Explainability & Accountability Lab. At NeuroTechSC I led the Machine Learning and Data team, connecting signal processing, model training, and live application work.

experience.description: Building evaluation machinery that makes autonomous-agent performance measurable, as described in my public introduction to the role.

experience.role: Machine Learning and Data Team Lead
experience.description: Led the ML and Data team in student neurotechnology research, including surface-EMG processing, model training, and live inference integration.
Collaborated on an early generative-AI enterprise platform using Django, language-model integrations, and AWS deployment.

collaborationParagraphs: I use coding agents as collaborators in implementation, experimentation, and review. My responsibility is to define the question, understand the system, inspect the evidence, and decide what the result supports. Project pages distinguish my work, team contributions, and upstream libraries.

The Studio makes that collaboration visible through creative tools, games, and simulations developed with GPT and Claude. Across research and products, I keep failures and limitations close to the results so that someone else can assess the work.
I'm interested in research and engineering collaborations around capable models, useful evaluation, reliable systems, and tools that help people understand and create.
